column1: # Cairene Egyptian cardinals, the values whose word differs from the Standard Arabic oblique form.
# Pronunciation: Adolf Dirr, Colloquial Egyptian Arabic Grammar, for the Use of Tourists, translated by
# W. H. Lyall, 1904, printed pages 24 and 26, in the book's own transcription.
# READ THE SOURCE'S AGE. It is a tourist grammar of 1904 and the only openly readable Egyptian source
# found, and its letters are not a phonemic transcription: it prints one consonant sign for sounds that
# its own numerals spell with ayn elsewhere. So the Arabic spelling of every row here is not read off
# Dirr's letters. It is the form written in modern transcripts, counted whole-word with an optional
# attached article or conjunction, and the counts are on the row, per corpus and never pooled: masc is
# the Massive Arabic Speech Corpus, which is Egyptian-leaning, sada is Saudi broadcast speech, omni is
# the Arabic dialect set of Omnilingual ASR. Every skeleton Dirr prints is still written today, which is
# what makes a 1904 source usable at all; where the modern corpus writes a different skeleton the row
# says so and the modern one is shipped.
# masc writes every ta marbuta as ha (ثلاثه 2338 against ثلاثة 0, and مئة 0), so it cannot choose between
# the two spellings of a word and its count for a ta-marbuta form is quoted from its ha spelling. The
# ta marbuta is shipped, which is the ordinary orthography and what the diacritizer expects.
